title: Deployable verification and versioned performance profiles
creator: Asha Patel
description: Create an automated, deployable process that publishes Redwood-verified performance profiles (latency, throughput, cost) for models and ties them to pinned model versions. The flow should support continuous verification, automated rollback of published profiles when regressions are detected, and a lightweight approval step for high-impact changes.
background: Currently profile publication is partly manual: verification runs are kicked off by SRE/research, results are collated, and PMs or owners push profiles to the catalog with ad-hoc notes. This causes delays, inconsistent metadata, and difficulty tracing profile -> model version lineage. As Dedicated and Private customers adopt custom pins, we need a deterministic, auditable publish workflow that supports version pinning and quick revert on regressions.
proposal: Build a publish pipeline that: (1) standardizes verified profile artifacts (JSON) with schema v2, (2) attaches profile to a model-version identifier and an optional pinned-release tag, (3) runs a staged publish: canary -> full catalog, (4) continuously monitors key metrics for 48h post-publish and auto-rolls back if regression thresholds hit, and (5) surfaces an approval UI in Console for >P1-impact changes.
scope: Implement verification-to-publish pipeline for open models in the catalog (initially Llama-3-family and Mistral variants), integrate with CI to produce signed profile artifacts, add Console UI for review + rollback, and add audit log entries for every publish action.
out_of_scope: Extending pipeline to private/on-prem customer-managed catalogs, and full integration with third-party benchmarking tools (will be tracked as follow-ups).
success_metrics: Time-to-publish (verification completion -> published) reduced from median 3 days to <6 hours
Number of manual edits to profile metadata before publish reduced by 80%
Post-publish regression rollbacks correctly triggered for >=90% of injected-regression test cases
Traceability: 100% of published profiles have model-version and CI run metadata attached
acceptance_criteria: Profile artifact schema v2 defined and documented in Confluence
CI job that produces a signed profile JSON from verification runs exists and is green on sample models
Publish pipeline can create canary entries in the catalog and optionally promote to full catalog via Console or API
Console shows pending publishes with diffs, approver, and timeline; approvals are auditable
Automated monitoring detects regressions (latency + 99th pct) and triggers rollback within configured thresholds
All publish/rollback actions produce entries in audit logs with trace IDs and links to verification runs
Rollback operation restores previous catalog entry and re-tags pinned versions accordingly
tasks: Define profile artifact schema v2 and mapping from verification outputs (latency p50/p95, throughput @batchX, cost-per-1k-tokens)
Add signing step to verification CI to produce immutable artifacts (SLSA-lite metadata)
Implement publish pipeline service that ingests signed artifacts and writes to the profile catalog (canary/full) with metadata
Console: build publish review panel with diff viewer, approver selection, and publish/promote/rollback buttons
Monitoring: hook profile publish to the runtime telemetry dashboard to create a 48h post-publish monitor and alert rules
Implement rollback orchestration that reverses catalog entry and notifies stakeholders
Integrate audit logs with centralized compliance system (link logs to customer-facing incidents when needed)
Run canary publish for two sample models and validate rollback by injecting latency regression in a testbed
risks: False positives from monitoring could cause unnecessary rollbacks and churn; we need precise thresholds and manual override
Signed artifacts must be protected; a leak/compromise could allow forged profiles — requires KMS integration and key rotation
Automation complexity: pipeline bugs could create stale or incorrect metadata in catalog leading to customer issues
Scope creep: adding private/on-prem customer catalog support will increase compliance burden

2025-02-20: Design provided two UX flows: minimal (auto) and review-first (manual approve) — default to review-first for P1 changes
